title: Beak shape, not body size, tells penguin species apart
subtitle: An A0 conference poster: one 3D scatter with its 2D twin as the central figure, three short columns and one stat tile
data: Palmer penguins: Gorman, Williams and Fraser (2014), PLoS ONE 9(3): e90081; Palmer Station LTER; via the palmerpenguins R package and vega-datasets 2.8.0 (CC0)
alt: An A0 portrait poster on white with cream cards. Headline: beak shape, not body size, tells penguin species apart. The central figure is a 3D scatter of beak depth, beak length and flipper length for 342 penguins of three species, with its beak-length against beak-depth twin beside it. Stat tile: 94 % of birds are placed in their own species by beak length and depth (leave-one-out nearest species mean), against 63 % by body mass alone.
note: Figure and every number by examples/python/poster/make_poster_figures.py (light, scale 2.6 on 2.6 x V.size('poster'), placed at 1:1); built by examples/latex/poster/build.py. QR code to https://akaminas.github.io/vellum/ by the qrcode package.
